name: True-Name Magic
laws: To know a thing's true name is to have power over it
True names are in the Old Speech; one cannot lie in it
Magic disturbs Equilibrium; the mage accepts the cost
costs: Self: the mage is changed by use
Knowledge: the true name, once known, must be kept
limits: A name must be learned; it cannot be guessed
Misusing a name returns the cost to the user
Some things (Nameless Ones) are older than the name-system and cannot be bound
examples: A Wizard of Earthsea — Ged learning his own true name

name: Gethenian Ambisexuality
laws: Gethenians are sexually neutral most of the time (somer)
During kemmer, they become reproductively polarized, either pole
No permanent sex; no gendered division of labor
costs: Reader must rebuild assumption about gender
Society organized around a cyclical biology
limits: Outsiders (Hainish visitors) are 'perverts' — always in one pole
examples: The Left Hand of Darkness — Genly Ai's confusion across the novel
